fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.

fields.label: Notation

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: in Hamilton's original derivation, additive fitness effects and weak selection; in the general form, b and c are partial regressions of fitness on the actor's and the partner's genotype

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: proved; exact in the regression form (Gardner, West and Wild 2011). Critics argue that the general form is close to an identity with little predictive content (Nowak, Tarnita and Wilson 2010).

fields.value: In a cooperative system (social insects, cooperatively breeding birds, microbes), estimate r from genotypes and b and c from fitness measurements, and test whether rb > c predicts which individuals help.
